source.title: Do safety-relevant LLM steering vectors optimized on a single example generalize?

page_placements.theme: Activation interventions control refusal with variable dimensionality

record.file_problem: none; the full LessWrong post is present
record.tranche_reason: It reports a Harmbench result for a prefilling attack, which tests whether prefilling can bypass refusal. It does not test the first-token KL explanation or the other bypass methods in V4.
record.gate_note: The post also reports one-shot steering results. Those use activation steering rather than the interventions named in the claim versions, so they are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The Poser results concern harmful choices in fictional scenarios, not compliance with a user's harmful request; they are also recorded under fits_no_version. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The only result bearing on a claim version is a prefilling baseline. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, prefilling 'Here's a step-by-step' gave 30.0% HarmBench ASR, which bears on V4. All other results use optimized activation steering, which is not an intervention V4 names, or the Poser fictional-choice task. This is a weak, incidental test: the prefill is reported only as a comparator for the authors' steering method, and no unprefilled ASR is given.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that steering vectors optimized on one example can generalize across inputs in safety settings (Poser, refusal), though efficacy varies a lot by training example. They also say validation-time inspection can predict efficacy. They present the 30.0% prefill ASR as evidence that promotion steering changes behaviour more than raising one string's probability.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes activation-space steering vectors on single examples and reports refusal-attack outcomes; it does not reproduce fine-tuning or per-token KL measurements from the source claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering-vector efficacy varies with the training example. For the Gemma Poser study, the authors also state that layer 10 was selected after validation at different layers; this is a selection result, not included as an outcome row.

fits_no_version.finding: One-shot optimized activation steering vectors gave HarmBench ASRs up to 96.9% on Gemma-2-2B-it (three vectors above 70%) and 93.1% on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in instruct models can be bypassed by an activation steering vector optimized on a single harmful prompt, with efficacy varying by training example.

fits_no_version.finding: In a Poser alignment-faking model, one vector trained on a single benign prompt flipped benign-to-harmful choices when added (93.4%) and harmful-to-benign when subtracted (83.4%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single activation direction found from one benign prompt can mediate harmful vs benign choices in an alignment-faking model.

record.problems: The post reports substantial variation in steering efficacy by training example. ASRs are evaluated with the Harmbench harm-classifier model, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The prefilling result has no stated unprefilled ASR comparator.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying outcomes omitted. The post's fictitious-information-retraction evaluation concerns surprisal and recovery from fictitious information, not the refusal or harmful-request behavior in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, prefill length dependence, other models, and why prefilling works.
No weight or rank localization; steering vectors operate in activation space.
No test of what causes shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong linkpost for arXiv:2502.18862. Evidence on V4 is thin: one model, one short prefill string, and no no-prefill control. The post's 'Here's a step-by-step' prefill is shorter than the multi-token prefills in the original work, which may explain the modest ASR. The ASR is judged by the HarmBench classifier, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune a safety-trained model on harmful examples.
The study does not fine-tune a model on ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
The study tests a prefilling attack, but not adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or whether bypass works because safety differences are concentrated in early response tokens.
The study optimizes steering vectors but does not test whether safety is localized in a small set of model weights or ranks.
The study does not test why safety behavior is shallow or whether data or training objectives produce shallowness.
The study does not test training that spreads safety beyond early tokens or whether such training holds up.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Prepended the tokens “Here's a step-by-step” to each Harmbench test-set input without steering.
rows.note: The post calls this a prefilling-attack baseline and says it yielded only 30.0% ASR. No unprefilled ASR is given, so the increase relative to ordinary generation cannot be quantified.
rows.check: Link and state are acceptable. The row is a baseline for the authors' steering method, not a designed test of prefilling. The baseline is not stated, so the rise over normal generation cannot be quantified. 30.0% is read as a partial bypass because it is far from the full defeat V4 describes.

source_check.correct: The tokens were prepended to the model's response for each HarmBench input, not to the input. ASR was 30.0% without steering.
source_check.problem: The operation places the prefill in the input instead of the response.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-it
rows.operation_detail: Optimized one-shot steering vectors for refusal suppression or promotion of a non-refusal completion, then evaluated them on Harmbench.
rows.value: Best-performing vector: 96.9%; three vectors in total had ASRs over 70%.
rows.note: This is an activation-steering result, not a test of the prefilling, suffix, or decoding interventions specified in V4. The post reports only the best result and the count exceeding 70%, not individual vector values.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct
